audit_finding: Mission exists, but repository-facing identity is still primarily Meridian rather than MINCO.
The repository contains more than a dashboard, but remains prototype-oriented and result-file driven.
The modeled problem directly addresses network capacity, transfers, unsafe excess, and demand uncertainty.
Stakeholders are documented in the specification but not represented through roles, workflows, or user research.
Transfers, surge capacity, and elective control are supported; staffing, bed assignment, discharge prioritization, and broader scheduling are not.
Several synthetic outcome metrics are demonstrated, but real operational value and production quality are not validated.
Modularity and explainability appear in places; testing, replaceability, configuration, and production discipline are inconsistent.
Prospective forecasting, scenarios, simulation, and recommendations exist on synthetic instances.
The platform does not perform clinical decisions, but it has no real integration layer for EHR/ADT/staffing systems.
Target users are described, but no role-specific authorization, interface validation, or user workflows exist.
An end-to-end prototype pipeline from operational inputs to recommendation and monitoring exists.
Prediction, simulation, optimization, and explanation are combined, but enterprise integration and production readiness are absent.
Subsystem folders exist, but runtime coupling remains high and the dashboard directly imports analytical code.
Prediction, risk, scenarios, simulation, optimization, decision, explanation, dashboard, API, and audit modules exist at uneven maturity; ingestion and observability do not.
Single responsibility is visible in some modules, but empty packages, monolithic dashboard code, and direct imports weaken the architecture.
Module interactions exist in code, but stable contracts, schemas, and integration tests are missing.
CSV loading and limited checks exist; no lineage, versioned datasets, feature service, streaming ingestion, or quality monitoring.
Markov and supervised forecasting code and results exist; operational validation is incomplete.
A stochastic network-state simulator exists, but not continuous state reconstruction or a true event-driven hospital twin.
Monte Carlo state-transition simulation exists; discrete-event simulation and historical calibration are absent.
A continuous LP and several policy wrappers exist; formal stochastic/robust/multi-objective formulations remain incomplete.
A policy-scoring and explanation pipeline creates recommendations, assumptions, and trade-off narratives.
Logical layers are present but not cleanly separated; frontend and command center directly import solver code.
A domain-oriented structure exists, but includes empty placeholders, generated files, and result bloat.
The documented FastAPI entry point is incorrect and the target module is empty.
What-if parsing and templated diagnosis exist, but the interface is not a general grounded analytical copilot.
Forecast, policy, sensitivity, and recommendation explanations exist, largely through templates and derived comparisons.
Two JSON modes exist, but many thresholds, policy rules, hospital names, and event presets remain hard-coded.
No authentication, authorization, audit-user identity, secrets management, or encryption configuration is implemented.
No service, data, model, optimization, simulation, or copilot monitoring stack is present.
Synthetic experiments, statistical tables, and stored pipeline logs exist; external and operational validation do not.
The test target exists but the test files are empty and pytest collects no tests.
Model files, CSV registries, and pipeline logs exist; no controlled registry, deployment lifecycle, drift monitoring, rollback, or retraining system.
No container, staging, production, cloud, or rollback deployment implementation is present.
No CI/CD workflow, linting gate, static analysis configuration, security scan, or automated release process is present.
Operational observability requirements are not implemented.
Governance is described but no privacy or access-control implementation exists.
README, architecture, executive summary, resume bullets, and research package exist; data, API, testing, deployment, and user documentation are incomplete.
No enforceable quality gates or release checklist automation exists.
Many analytical prototype components exist, but testing, deployment, security, ingestion, observability, and production APIs do not meet the completion definition.
Research-oriented experiments and manuscript tables exist, but claims are based on synthetic data and several methods need stronger validation.
The repository is clearly positioned as the healthcare flagship in documents, though portfolio governance artifacts are not embedded in the archive.
Executive summaries, architecture explanations, and resume bullets support interview narratives.
No license, contribution guide, issue templates, release process, or open-source governance files are present.
Commercialization is a target only; no multi-tenant, integration, security, or deployment foundation exists.
RL and advanced AI experiments exist, but the listed future capabilities are not production platform features.
No versioned implementation evolution or release history is present.
The specification governs the project conceptually, but repository-level architecture decisions and changes are not consistently recorded.
Synthetic technical and decision metrics exist; operational, product, deployment, and user-trust metrics do not.
The repository demonstrates a substantial prototype, not the enterprise-grade platform described by the conclusion.
